claims.text: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization.
Single-phase fcc FeCoNi or closely related high-entropy derivatives have coercivity no greater than approximately 100 Oe.
Adding a few atomic percent Ga to fcc FeCoNi will promote formation of a predominantly fcc dual-phase microstructure containing a minor BCC fraction.
The minor BCC phase will occur as well-dispersed precipitates embedded in the fcc matrix.
Vacuum arc melting is a viable route for producing FeCoNi-based alloys whose phase constitution is modified by a minor additive.
Homogenization annealing at around 673 K will stabilize the proposed Ga-induced dual-phase structure.
Interfaces between the fcc matrix and BCC precipitates will create local magnetic-anisotropy variations.
Microstructural changes and enhanced magnetic anisotropy can strengthen domain-wall pinning and increase coercivity.
The proposed fcc/BCC interfaces will impede domain-wall movement.
Ga-doped FeCoNi will have coercivity exceeding 100 Oe relative to the single-phase control.
Ga-doped FeCoNi will retain high saturation magnetization after formation of the minor BCC phase.
A low Ga concentration can create a limited BCC fraction without drastically changing overall composition or sacrificing the characteristic high saturation magnetization.
XRD and TEM will be used to test whether the doped alloy contains a minor BCC phase.
Room-temperature SQUID or VSM hysteresis measurements will compare coercivity and saturation magnetization between identically processed undoped and Ga-doped batches.

contradictions.description: The conditions restrict magnetic characterization to low applied fields, while the experiment and outcome require determination of saturation magnetization, which ordinarily requires a field sufficient to approach magnetic saturation.
